\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Config Graph: Results}

\begin{definition}[Output summary classes]
\lean{Turing.OutSummary}
\label{Turing.OutSummary}
\leanok
Let the output summary have three classes: empty, meaning that nothing has been emitted;
accepting, meaning that the output is exactly the one-symbol string $[\mathrm{true}]$;
and dead, meaning that the output can no longer become $[\mathrm{true}]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output summary]
\lean{Turing.outSummary}
\label{Turing.outSummary}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OutSummary}
For a finite Boolean string $w$, its output summary is empty if $w$ is empty, accepting
if $w=[\mathrm{true}]$, and dead in every other case.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Accept summary characterisation]
\lean{Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff}
\label{Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite Boolean string $u$, its output summary is the accepting summary if and
only if $u$ is exactly the one-bit string $[1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty summary characterisation]
\lean{Turing.outSummary_eq_empty_iff}
\label{Turing.outSummary_eq_empty_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite Boolean string $u$, its output summary is the empty summary if and only
if $u$ is empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Append preserves output summaries]
\lean{Turing.outSummary_append_congr}
\label{Turing.outSummary_append_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary}
\difficulty{5}
For finite Boolean strings $u$, $v$, and $e$, if $u$ and $v$ have the same output
summary, then appending $e$ to each gives strings with the same output summary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Output summary code]
\lean{Turing.outSummaryCode}
\label{Turing.outSummaryCode}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.OutSummary}
Assign the codes $0$, $1$, and $2$ in $\text{Fin}(3)$ to the empty, accepting, and dead
output summaries, respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the Summary Code]
\lean{Turing.outSummaryCode_injective}
\label{Turing.outSummaryCode_injective}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummaryCode}
\difficulty{4}
The map assigning a code in $\{0,1,2\}$ to each of the three output-summary values is
injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Representative summary strings]
\lean{Turing.summaryWord}
\label{Turing.summaryWord}
\leanok
For $\tau\in\text{Fin}(3)$, associate the empty Boolean string if $\tau=0$, the string
$[\mathrm{true}]$ if $\tau=1$, and the string $[\mathrm{false}]$ if $\tau=2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Decoding Summary Words]
\lean{Turing.outSummaryCode_summaryWord}
\label{Turing.outSummaryCode_summaryWord}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode, Turing.summaryWord}
\difficulty{2}
For every code $\tau\in\{0,1,2\}$, the output summary of its associated summary word has
code $\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Updated output summary code]
\lean{Turing.summaryTag}
\label{Turing.summaryTag}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode, Turing.summaryWord}
Given $\tau\in\text{Fin}(3)$ and an optional Boolean symbol $b$, append $b$ if present
to the representative string for $\tau$, take the output summary of the resulting
string, and return its code in $\text{Fin}(3)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Identity under the empty update]
\lean{Turing.summaryTag_none}
\label{Turing.summaryTag_none}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummaryCode_summaryWord, Turing.summaryTag}
\difficulty{1}
For every $\tau \in \mathrm{Fin}(3)$, the summary tag obtained by appending no symbol to
the word representing $\tau$ equals $\tau$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Summary update under appending a bit]
\lean{Turing.summaryTag_append}
\label{Turing.summaryTag_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode, Turing.outSummaryCode_injective, Turing.outSummaryCode_summaryWord, Turing.outSummary_append_congr, Turing.summaryTag}
\difficulty{2}
Encode a summary tag $0$ by the empty word, $1$ by the one-letter word
$[\mathrm{true}]$, and $2$ by $[\mathrm{false}]$. Summarize a Boolean word as empty if
it is empty, accepting if it is exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, and dead otherwise, with
these three summaries coded by $0,1,2$, respectively. For every Boolean word $u$ and
optional Boolean symbol $b$, the code of the summary of $u$ followed by $b$ (if present)
equals the summary tag obtained from the code of the summary of $u$ and $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Code One Characterizes Acceptance]
\lean{Turing.outSummaryCode_eq_one_iff}
\label{Turing.outSummaryCode_eq_one_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode, Turing.outSummaryCode_injective, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $u$, the code of its output summary equals $1$ if and only if $u$
is the one-symbol word containing true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Code of the Empty Output]
\lean{Turing.outSummaryCode_nil}
\label{Turing.outSummaryCode_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode}
\difficulty{1}
The code of the output summary of the empty word is $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounds for an in-window configuration]
\lean{Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds}
\label{Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a type, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $s$ be a
natural number, and let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$. Suppose
every work-tape head is at distance at most $s$ from the origin, and every cell at
distance greater than $s$ from the origin is blank. Then each work-tape head is at
distance at most $s$ from the origin, and every nonblank cell on every work tape is at
distance at most $s$ from the origin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Core configuration with output summary]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.coreSum}
\label{Turing.NDTM.coreSum}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.OutSummary, Turing.outSummary}
For a configuration of a $k$-tape Turing machine on a fixed Boolean input, form the
ordered pair consisting of its core configuration data (state, input-head position,
work-tape contents, and work-head positions) and the output summary of its output
string.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One-step configuration transition]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.CfgStep}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p002-b002}
\label{Turing.NDTM.CfgStep}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
For a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols and state set $S$, and
configurations $c,c'$ on the same input, define $c'$ to be a one-step successor of $c$
if there is a choice bit $b\in\{0,1\}$ for which the machine's transition using $b$
takes $c$ to $c'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Finite runs and transition reachability]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff}
\label{Turing.NDTM.reflTransGen_cfgStep_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.CfgStep, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and
let $c,c'$ be configurations of $M$ on the same input. There is a finite sequence of
zero or more single steps, each made using some choice bit, from $c$ to $c'$ if and only
if there is a finite Boolean word $w$ such that running $M$ from $c$ under $w$ yields
$c'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Output Depends Only on Core Configuration Data]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.outputSymbol_congr}
\label{Turing.NDTM.outputSymbol_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.outputSymbol}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a deterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a
Boolean input word, and let $c,d$ be configurations on that input. If their states,
input-head positions, work-tape contents, and work-tape head positions agree, then the
optional symbol emitted by one step of $M$ from $c$ equals the optional symbol emitted
from $d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Core data after one choice]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_output, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.outputSymbol_congr, Turing.NDTM.stepWith, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step, Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummary_append_congr}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
let $b$ be a Boolean choice, and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. If two configurations
on $x$ have the same state, input-head position, work-tape contents and work-tape head
positions, and their output words have the same summary (empty, exactly
$[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to become $[\mathrm{true}]$), then after one step
under $b$ their resulting configurations have the same such core data and output
summary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Core data after a choice word]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_stepWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols and $k$ work tapes,
and let $x$ be a Boolean input word. If two configurations on $x$ have the same state,
input-head position, work-tape contents and work-tape head positions, and their output
words have the same summary (empty, exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to become
$[\mathrm{true}]$), then running both configurations under any choice word yields
configurations with the same such core data and output summary.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One Additional Run Step]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.take_succ_action}
\label{Turing.NDTM.take_succ_action}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.runWith_nil, Turing.NDTM.stepWith_eq_fixChoice_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean symbols, and
state set $S$, and fix a Boolean input string $x$. For every choice word $w$ and every
$j\in\mathbb{N}$, the configuration reached from $c$ by running $M$ on the prefix of $w$
of length $j+1$ is either the configuration reached by running $M$ on the prefix of
length $j$, or is obtained by applying a single action to that latter configuration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Visited head positions bound their magnitude]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.abs_lt_card_visitedWith}
\label{Turing.NDTM.abs_lt_card_visitedWith}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.abs_lt_card_image_of_unitSteps, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.take_succ_action, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith, Turing.workTapePos_apply_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean work-tape alphabet
and state set $S$, let $w$ be a finite binary choice word, and let $i$ be a work-tape
index. If an integer $z$ occurs as the position of head $i$ in a configuration reached
from the initial configuration on input $x$ by running under some prefix of $w$, then
$|z|$ is strictly less than the number of distinct positions of head $i$ reached by
running under prefixes of $w$ (including the empty prefix and all prefixes of length at
most $|w|$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Written Cells Were Visited]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none}
\label{Turing.NDTM.mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.mem_image_workTapePos_of_ne_none, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.take_succ_action, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and Boolean tape
symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $w$ be a finite choice word, let $i$ be a
work-tape index, and let $z\in\mathbb{Z}$. If cell $z$ on tape $i$ contains a symbol
after running $M$ from its initial configuration on $x$ under $w$, then $z$ is among the
head positions visited on tape $i$ during that run, including the initial position and
the positions after each of the first $|w|$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Visited Positions on a Prefix]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_take_subset}
\label{Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_take_subset}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w$ be a finite
binary word, let $c$ be a configuration on a fixed input, let $j$ be a nonnegative
integer, and choose a work tape $i$. Every head position visited on tape $i$ during the
run under the prefix of $w$ of length $j$ is also visited during the run under $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Runs remain within a space window]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow}
\label{Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.abs_lt_card_visitedWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.mem_visitedWith_of_ne_none, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith, Turing.NDTM.visitedWith_take_subset}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine with Boolean input and state set
$S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $w$ be a choice word. If the space used by
the run under $w$ from the initial configuration on $x$ is at most $s\in\mathbb{N}$,
then for every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ the configuration reached under the prefix of $w$ of
length $j$ lies in the window of radius $s$: every work-tape head position has absolute
value at most $s$, and every cell at an integer position with absolute value greater
than $s$ is blank on every work tape.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Window membership from core-summary equality]
\lean{Turing.NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq}
\label{Turing.NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.NDTM.coreSum}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $c,d$ be
configurations on $x$ for a machine with $k$ work tapes and state set $S$. If they have
the same state, input-head position, work-tape contents and head positions, and their
output words have the same summary (empty, exactly $[\mathrm{true}]$, or unable ever to
become $[\mathrm{true}]$), then if every work-tape head of $d$ lies within distance $s$
of the origin and every cell of each work tape outside that interval is blank, the same
properties hold for $c$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.coreSum_runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input $x$, state set
$S$, and configuration $c$ on $x$. Let $w$ be a finite choice word and let $a,b$ be
natural numbers with $a\le b\le |w|$. Suppose that the configurations reached after the
first $a$ and first $b$ choices have the same core data and the same output summary. If
the middle segment of choices from positions $a$ through $b$ is deleted, the resulting
run has the same core data and output summary as the run under all of $w$. Moreover,
every prefix of the shortened choice word has the same core data and output summary as
some prefix of $w$, whose length is at most $|w|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Configuration bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet, with
$N.k$ work tapes, and natural numbers $n$ and $s$, define its configuration bound by
\[3\bigl(|Q|+1\bigr)(n+2)\,3^{N.k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^{N.k},\]
where $|Q|$ is the number of states of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on Windowed Configurations]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.count_windowed_vertices}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.count_windowed_vertices}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.coreCode_inj, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.outSummary, Turing.outSummaryCode, Turing.outSummaryCode_injective}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let
$x$ be a binary input, and let $s,t\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $(c_j)_{j\in\mathbb{N}}$ is a
sequence of configurations on input $x$, each of the first $t+1$ configurations has
every work-tape head within distance $s$ of the origin and has blank contents outside
that window, and the configurations have distinct cores together with output summaries
for indices $0,\ldots,t$. Then $t+1\le 3(|Q|+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$, where $Q$ is
the state set and $k$ is the number of work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No acceptance in zero steps]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.not_acceptsWithin_zero}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.not_acceptsWithin_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let
$x$ be a binary input. There is no choice word of length zero for which the run from the
initial configuration on $x$ halts with output exactly the one-bit string $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance under a space bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.InWindow, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound, Turing.FinNDTM.count_windowed_vertices, Turing.NDTM.coreSum, Turing.NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_take_inWindow, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith, Turing.NDTM.splice_vertices, Turing.outSummary_eq_accept_iff}
\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let
$x$ be a Boolean input, and let $T,s\in\mathbb{N}$. If some choice word of length
exactly $T$ makes $N$ halt on $x$ with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, and every choice word
of length exactly $T$ uses at most $s$ work-tape cells in total on that input, then some
choice word of length exactly $3\bigl(|Q|+1\bigr)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s+1)}(2s+1)^k$ makes $N$
halt on $x$ with output $[\mathrm{true}]$, where $Q$ is the state set and $k$ is the
number of work tapes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance implies language membership]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_of_acceptsWithin}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_of_acceptsWithin}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin.mono, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $s\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for
every binary input $y$ there is a time bound under which $N$ halts on every branch, uses
at most $s(|y|)$ work-tape cells on every branch, and accepts $y$ exactly when $y\in L$.
If a binary string $x$ is accepted by $N$ within $t$ steps for some $t\in\mathbb{N}$,
then $x\in L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership and acceptance at the configuration bound]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInSpace.mem_of_acceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_of_spaceUsedWith_le, Turing.FinNDTM.configBound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be
a language of binary strings, and let $s\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for
every input $x$ there is a time $T$ such that $N$ halts on every branch by time $T$,
uses at most $s(|x|)$ work-tape cells on every branch of length $T$, and $x\in L$
exactly when $N$ accepts $x$ within $T$ steps. Then, for every binary string $x$, $x\in
L$ if and only if $N$ accepts $x$ within $3(\lvert
Q\rvert+1)(|x|+2)3^{k(2s(|x|)+1)}(2s(|x|)+1)^k$ steps, where $Q$ is the state set of $N$
and $k$ is its number of work tapes.
\end{theorem}
